sourcedFrom: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual (2026 (copyright line, printed p.14))
cleanIntro: The TiTrex 260Ti is the 6.5 mm titanium-core TiTrex, and Precision Armament's own TiTrex installation and maintenance manual covers it. The can is three pieces an owner handles: the 3D-printed core inside its serialized XBand housing, the mount threaded onto the rear, and the Universal Front Cap or K-Brake threaded onto the front, with two Universal Wrenches in the box for assembly and disassembly. Precision Armament calls the core largely self-cleaning on centerfire and asks mainly that the thread interfaces be kept clean. The core itself is never opened: when it is worn or damaged it goes back to the factory and is exchanged whole. The book's rating sentence describes the TiTrex line as a whole; the 260Ti is the 6.5 mm bore, and the caliber marked on your can is the limit.

steps.title: Unloaded, action open, before the can is touched
steps.action: Unload the host, open the action, look in the chamber and take out any magazine before the suppressor is attached or removed. Precision Armament puts this first in its book and repeats it at the head of both the mounting and the removal pages. If you are unsure how to clear the host, its own maker's manual is the authority.
steps.prose: Every removal on this can is wrench work right in front of the muzzle.
steps.quote: Verify the firearm is unloaded and the action is open before attaching or removing the suppressor.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — WARNING & SAFETY INFORMATION, p.2
steps.warn: Chamber checked by eye, magazine out, action open.

steps.title: Let it cool, or wear heat-resistant gloves
steps.action: The TiTrex soaks up a lot of heat while firing and stays hot well after. Give it time to cool, or handle it only in heat-resistant gloves, and set it down on something that cannot burn or melt.
steps.prose: The book repeats this on the removal page.
steps.quote: Allow adequate time for cooling, or wear heat-resistant gloves to avoid burns.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, removing the suppressor, p.8
steps.warn: Hot cans burn. Wait, or wear heat-resistant gloves.

steps.title: No exposed-lead ammunition through it
steps.action: Precision Armament bars unjacketed and exposed-lead bullets from this can: lead deposits cannot be cleaned out of it and may permanently affect its performance. Know what has been fired through it before you clean, and keep lead bullets out of it from here on.
steps.prose: No cleaning method in the book removes lead, so the only cure is never to fire it.
steps.quote: Do not use ammunition with unjacketed or exposed lead bullets.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — AMMUNITION GUIDELINES, p.3

steps.title: Support the rifle
steps.action: Put the rifle in a stable rest or brace it so it cannot shift while you work. Breaking the can free takes a wrench and real force, and a rifle that moves under it drags the muzzle somewhere you did not mean.
steps.prose: This is the book's first removal step.
steps.quote: Place the rifle in a stable rest or brace it securely so it cannot shift while you remove the suppressor.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, removing the suppressor, item 1, p.8

steps.title: Break it free with the wrench on the mount slots
steps.action: Put one of the Universal Wrenches on the wrench slots of the mount and break the suppressor free from the barrel. The wrench goes on the mount, not on the suppressor body: Precision Armament warns that a wrench on the body can unscrew the core from the mount and leave the mount stuck on the barrel.
steps.prose: Feel for the joint at the barrel letting go, not the core turning on the mount.
steps.quote: Place the wrench on the mount wrench slots to break the suppressor free from the barrel.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, removing the suppressor, item 2, p.8
steps.warn: Wrench on the mount slots, never on the body.

steps.title: Unscrew it by hand
steps.action: Once the mount is loose, unscrew the whole suppressor assembly from the barrel by hand, carefully, keeping it square so the threads are not dragged. The mount and the front cap or brake stay on the core for the routine clean.
steps.prose: If the mount stayed on the barrel, the wrench was on the body: the mount comes off the barrel with the wrench on its slots.
steps.quote: Once the mount is loose, carefully unscrew the suppressor assembly by hand.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, removing the suppressor, item 3, p.8

steps.title: Threads and mounting surfaces, solvent and a soft brush
steps.action: Clean the mount's threads and seating face and the host's muzzle threads and shoulder with a standard firearm solvent and a soft nylon or brass brush. Precision Armament asks for the thread interfaces to be kept clean regularly: carbon there is what stops the can seating tight against the shoulder.
steps.prose: A soft brush, as the book says: no steel on titanium threads.
steps.quote: Clean mounting surfaces and threads with a standard firearm solvent and a soft nylon or brass brush.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS, item 1, p.9

steps.title: A brush through the bore if it needs it — never a patch
steps.action: Look into the can for carbon and fouling. If it needs it, pass a cleaning brush through the bore to knock the fouling loose. Never push a patch through: Precision Armament warns a patch can lodge inside and cause a catastrophic failure on the next shot.
steps.prose: The book calls the core largely self-cleaning on centerfire, so often nothing is needed here.
steps.quote: If necessary, pass a cleaning brush (no patches) through the bore to dislodge fouling.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS, item 1, p.9

steps.title: Wipe the outside and oil it lightly
steps.action: Wipe down the outside with a firearm-specific cleaner, then put on a light layer of the firearm lubricant you use. Most rust-preventive oils are safe, though Precision Armament notes they may darken or change the finish. Keep chlorinated solvents, ammonia and acids off it: they can damage titanium.
steps.prose: Standard firearm cleaners and lubricants only, as the book asks.
steps.quote: Wipe down the exterior with a firearm-specific cleaner, and reapply a light layer of your choice of firearm lubricant.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS, item 2, p.9

steps.title: Nothing in the bore before it goes back on
steps.action: Look through the can from both ends before it goes back on the gun. Heavy fouling, a cleaning patch or anything else in the bore means it does not get fired: Precision Armament warns a blocked suppressor can be extremely dangerous.
steps.prose: One clean, round circle of light, centred, is what you want to see.
steps.quote: Inspect the suppressor for internal obstructions such as excessive fouling, cleaning patches, or any foreign objects before firing.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — WARNING & SAFETY INFORMATION, p.2
steps.warn: Anything in the bore: do not fire it.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The can is off the host, its thread interfaces and outside are clean, and the bore is clear. The mount and the front cap or K-Brake stayed on the core. Taking those two off to clean every TiTrex thread is the Deep Clean.
steps.prose: Reassembly for this path is the can back on the barrel and checked.
steps.quote: Care should be taken to regularly keep the suppressor thread interfaces clean.
steps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS, p.9

deepSteps.title: Mount and front cap off the core, with the two wrenches
deepSteps.action: With the can off the host, put one Universal Wrench on the mount and the other on the front cap or K-Brake and unscrew each from the core. Every TiTrex thread is a standard right-hand thread, so each turns counter-clockwise, seen from its own end, to come off. Keep the wrenches close together so one hand can clamp them, as the book shows for tightening.
deepSteps.prose: The two wrenches in the box are supplied for exactly this.
deepSteps.quote: Universal Wrenches (x2) — for proper assembly and disassembly.
deepSteps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — PRODUCT OVERVIEW, item 6, p.5

deepSteps.title: The core stays whole
deepSteps.action: That is as far as the TiTrex comes apart. The core and its serialized XBand housing are never taken apart or altered by the owner; Precision Armament says doing so voids the warranty and service eligibility. A core that is worn or damaged goes back to Precision Armament for a whole-core exchange.
deepSteps.prose: The core exchange is the maker's service, not a bench job.
deepSteps.quote: Never attempt to remove or modify the serialized component, as this will void your warranty and service eligibility.
deepSteps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — CORE EXCHANGES AND UPGRADES, item 2, p.10
deepSteps.warn: The serialized XBand stays on the core.

deepSteps.title: Every TiTrex thread clean and free of debris
deepSteps.action: Clean the threads on the core at both ends and the threads of the mount and the front cap or brake with a standard firearm solvent and a soft nylon or brass brush, until they are free of carbon and debris. The book asks for clean threads before each part goes back on.
deepSteps.prose: Clean threads are what let each joint reach its torque without galling.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure threads are clean and free of debris.
deepSteps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, item 1, p.6

deepSteps.title: The right chemistry, and good air
deepSteps.action: Use standard firearm cleaners only. Precision Armament warns that chlorinated solvents, ammonia and acids can damage titanium, and that many solvents are toxic and flammable: work where the air moves, wear gloves and eye protection, and keep solvent away from heat and flame.
deepSteps.prose: The warnings are on the book's maintenance page.
deepSteps.quote: Avoid cleaners containing chlorinated solvents, ammonia, or acids, which may damage titanium.
deepSteps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS, p.9
deepSteps.warn: No chlorinated solvents, ammonia or acids.

deepSteps.title: Mount back on by hand
deepSteps.action: Thread the mount onto the core by hand, square, taking care not to cross-thread it. Precision Armament recommends a small amount of anti-seize compound on all TiTrex threads before assembly.
deepSteps.prose: Hand tight first; the wrenches come last.
deepSteps.quote: Thread the mount onto the suppressor by hand.
deepSteps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, item 1, p.6

deepSteps.title: Front cap or K-Brake back on by hand
deepSteps.action: Thread the Universal Front Cap or the K-Brake onto the front of the core by hand, again with clean threads and no cross-threading.
deepSteps.prose: Whichever front piece you run goes on the same way.
deepSteps.quote: Thread the Universal Front Cap or K-Brake Ultracompact Suppressor Brake onto the suppressor by hand.
deepSteps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, item 2, p.6

deepSteps.title: Both tightened with the wrenches
deepSteps.action: Once both are hand tight, use the two wrenches to bring the mount and the front cap into their final position. Precision Armament gives 25 ft-lb, plus or minus 5, for the HUB mount, so that nothing loosens in use.
deepSteps.prose: Keep the wrenches close together so one hand can clamp them for leverage.
deepSteps.quote: Apply sufficient torque (25 ±5 ft-lbs for HUB Mount) to avoid loosening during use.
deepSteps.cite: TiTrex User Installation & Maintenance Manual — ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, item 3, p.6

cleaning.name: THREADS & MOUNTING SURFACES
tasks: Mount threads and seating face cleaned with a standard firearm solvent and a soft nylon or brass brush
The host's muzzle threads and shoulder cleaned the same way
Thread interfaces kept clean every time: carbon there stops the can seating against the shoulder

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Inspected for carbon buildup and fouling
If necessary, a cleaning brush through the bore to dislodge fouling
⛔ No cleaning patches through the bore: a lodged patch can cause a catastrophic failure

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & FINISH
tasks: Exterior wiped down with a firearm-specific cleaner
A light layer of firearm lubricant reapplied; rust-preventive oils may darken the finish
⛔ No cleaners containing chlorinated solvents, ammonia or acids: they may damage titanium

cleaning.name: WHILE YOU CLEAN
tasks: A well-ventilated area: many solvents are toxic and flammable
Solvents kept away from heat and flames

reassembly: Clean every TiTrex thread, and put a small amount of anti-seize compound on each, as Precision Armament recommends.
Thread the mount onto the core by hand, square, without cross-threading.
Thread the Universal Front Cap or the K-Brake onto the front of the core by hand.
With the two Universal Wrenches, tighten the mount and the front cap into their final position: 25 ft-lb, plus or minus 5, for the HUB mount.

Host unloaded and the action open: align the can with the barrel threads and thread it on by hand without cross-threading until it is firmly seated, then use one wrench to seat it properly against the barrel shoulder. A thread-locking compound such as Rocksett may be used on the barrel threads, following its own instructions.
Check alignment with an alignment rod made for your caliber. If the can is not concentric with the bore, stop and consult a qualified gunsmith.
fncheck: Before each use, the can is tight and seated against the barrel shoulder, as Precision Armament requires: a can that is not seated loses alignment and risks a baffle strike. The mount and the front cap or brake are tight on the core at the torque you set. An alignment rod for your caliber passes concentric with the bore, and the bore is clear of fouling, patches and anything else.
